tldr: Huabu is an open-source desktop workspace from Microsoft that replaces the linear chat window with an infinite canvas shared by a person and their AI agents. Ideas, files and agent results become visible, connected nodes in a Space, so people and agents work from the same organized context. Long Ling helped build it from 0 to 1 during her internship at Microsoft Research Asia.

facts.label: Platform
facts.value: Desktop app for macOS (Apple silicon) and Windows (x64)

facts.label: Status
facts.value: Released for research and experimental use

sections.heading: What is Huabu
paragraphs: Huabu calls itself “an infinite work surface” where you and your agents think together. Instead of a chat thread, it gives you a Space: a canvas where ideas, files, open questions and agents sit side by side. Everything stays visible and connected across sessions, and the stated goal is to turn clearer thinking into work that ships.

The project site makes a comparison with the desktop. The desktop gave files and programs one surface to meet; Huabu aims to do the same for the agent era, bringing thoughts, sources, tasks and results onto one shared thinking surface. The site sums this up as “the agent era gets its shell.”

sections.heading: Core Ideas
paragraphs: The design starts from a simple observation on the project site: chat is linear, but thinking is not. Three ideas follow from it.
bullets: Externalize anything: scattered ideas get one place where they become visible and connected, instead of staying buried in separate conversations.
Position is part of the thinking: where a node sits on the canvas carries meaning. Arranging research by time or direction is part of making sense of it, not decoration.
Shared context for people and agents: connected materials become readable context for both the user and their agents. Agents start their work from what is already in the Space.

sections.heading: Key Features
paragraphs: The README lists three core features, and the project site walks through the same workflow step by step.
bullets: Bring scattered information together: drag ideas, notes, documents and outputs from different chat sessions and sources into one Space.
Bring in anything: pull a thought from a conversation, or drop in a PDF, website, image, video or file. Each one becomes a node that can be placed, revisited and connected.
Organize your thinking with AI: arrange information, uncover relationships and clarify ideas with AI, while reviewing and controlling every proposed change.

Let agents work with richer context: bring your own agents into a Space. There they can see not only the materials you provide but also how those materials relate, which helps them grasp your intent and do more relevant work.
Put agents to work: give agents a brief, run tasks in parallel, and bring every result back to the Space.

sections.heading: How It Works
paragraphs: Huabu runs as a desktop application built on Electron. On first launch, the user picks a local folder as their Home, and Spaces and their materials are stored there. The desktop client normally runs with its own local server, but it can also connect to an existing remote Huabu Server. A standalone web mode serves the web app and API from a single Fastify process. By default it only accepts connections from the local machine; opening it to a network requires setting the bind address, the allowed hostnames and HTTP Basic Auth.

Huabu does not ship its own LLM service. Users configure a model provider of their choice and can connect external coding agents; the User Handbook covers both setups. When an AI feature is used, the provider may receive the prompt and the relevant Space content, and external agents may read or modify files in the working directory configured for them.
bullets: Local storage: Spaces and materials stay in the Home folder the user selects.
Protected credentials: packaged builds encrypt saved credentials using storage protected by the operating system.
No telemetry: Huabu does not send telemetry, crash reports, diagnostic logs or usage data to Microsoft.

sections.heading: Getting Started
paragraphs: Packaged apps are published on GitHub Releases. Download the package for your platform, open the .dmg on macOS or run the .exe installer on Windows, then launch Huabu and choose a Home folder. The Huabu User Handbook is the official guide to model setup, core concepts and creating a first Space.

Building from source requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm 10+. After installing dependencies, a single command starts the server, the web client and the shared package in watch mode, then opens Huabu in its own desktop window.

sections.heading: Responsible Use
paragraphs: Huabu is released for research and experimental use. The README notes that AI-generated output may be inaccurate, incomplete, biased or unsafe, and that the system has not been evaluated for every language, model or downstream scenario. It should not be used for high-risk or time-critical decisions, or in workflows where output is acted on without qualified human review. Materials in the repository are available under the MIT License.

sections.heading: My Role
paragraphs: Long Ling worked on Huabu during her internship at Microsoft Research Asia and helped build the system from 0 to 1. Her work explored new interaction paradigms for organizing knowledge, maintaining shared context, and letting agents take collaborative actions. These threads match the project's aim: a shared workspace where humans and agents can collect what matters, organize it together, and act on shared knowledge.
